title: Closed images and norm bounds for finite affinoid modules
statement: Let $K$ be a complete field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $A\ne0$ be a quotient of a restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], with a Tate quotient Banach norm $\|\cdot\|_A$. Let $M,N$ be finitely generated $A$-modules, each equipped with a complete nonarchimedean $K$-vector-space norm. Suppose their scalar actions are bounded: for some positive constants $c_M,c_N$, $\|am\|_M\le c_M\|a\|_A\|m\|_M$ and $\|an\|_N\le c_N\|a\|_A\|n\|_N$. Every $A$-linear map $u:M\to N$ is continuous and has closed image. If $u$ is injective, there exists a real $H>0$ such that $\|m\|_M\le H\|u(m)\|_N$ for every $m\in M$. Zero modules are permitted.

source.place: A little p-adic functional analysis (part 2 of 2), Lemma 1, PDF p.1, read online 2026-10-24; together with affinoid Noetherianity in Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry (2008), section 1.4 Proposition 2(i), and the Banach open mapping theorem. Archival copies WANTED; statement includes the standard finite-generator/open-mapping corollary.

proof.text: Write $D=K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle$ and choose the given quotient map $D\twoheadrightarrow A$. Apply [lem-trf-affinoid-polynomial-closed-point-comparison] with $F=K$ and the polynomial ideal $J=0$: its assertion that $C$ is Noetherian gives precisely that $D$ is Noetherian. For any ideal $I\subseteq A$, its inverse image in $D$ has finitely many generators; their images generate $I$. Hence $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The given Banach norm on $A$ makes every finite power $A^s$, with maximum norm, complete: each coordinate of a Cauchy sequence converges, and the finitely many coordinate limits give convergence in the maximum norm. If $M=0$ or $N=0$, the map is zero, is continuous, and has closed image $\{0\}$; injectivity then forces $M=0$ and $H=1$ works. Below assume $M,N\ne0$.

source.place: Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry (April 2008), section 1.4 Proposition 2(i), printed p.22 (PDF p.23), read online 2026-10-24. Tate Noetherianity supplied by the existing polynomial/affinoid comparison node at J=0. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose a nonempty finite generating family $e_1,\ldots,e_s$ of $M$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The surjection $p:A^s\to M$, $p(a)=\sum_i a_i e_i$, is $K$-linear and satisfies $\|p(a)-p(b)\|_M\le c_M\max_i\|e_i\|_M\max_i\|a_i-b_i\|_A$, so is continuous. Apply [lem-trf-banach-surjective-bounded-lifts] to the Banach $K$-spaces $A^s,M$. It supplies $L>0$ such that every $m$ has a representation $m=\sum_i a_i e_i$ with $\max_i\|a_i\|_A\le L\|m\|_M$. By $A$-linearity and the bound on the action on $N$, $\|u(m)\|_N\le c_N L\max_i\|u(e_i)\|_N\|m\|_M$. Applying the same inequality to $m-m'$ proves continuity of $u$.

source.place: Lemma 1, PDF p.1, read online 2026-10-24; agent expansion for bounded scalar actions, automatic continuity and the injective norm bound. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $S=u(M)$ and $B=\overline S\subseteq N$. Addition, negation and multiplication by each fixed $a\in A$ preserve limits, the last by the scalar-action bound. Thus $B$ is an $A$-submodule. It is complete: a Cauchy sequence in $B$ converges in $N$, and its limit lies in the closure $B$. If $B=0$ then $S=B$. Otherwise [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], applied to $B\subseteq N$ over the Noetherian ring from step 1, supplies generators $b_1,\ldots,b_t$, $t>0$. The surjection $A^t\to B$ defined by these generators is continuous by the same finite-sum estimate as in step 2. Apply [lem-trf-banach-surjective-bounded-lifts] to obtain $L_B>0$ such that every $x\in B$ is $\sum_i a_i b_i$ with $\max_i\|a_i\|_A\le L_B\|x\|_N$. Fix $0<\theta<1$ and, by density, $f_i\in S$ with $\|b_i-f_i\|_N<\theta/(c_N L_B)$. For $x_0=x\in B$, recursively choose such coefficients $a_{ji}$ for $x_j$ and put $x_{j+1}=x_j-\sum_i a_{ji}f_i=\sum_i a_{ji}(b_i-f_i)$. The action bound gives $\|x_{j+1}\|_N\le\theta\|x_j\|_N$, hence $\|a_{ji}\|_A\le L_B\theta^j\|x\|_N$. For fixed $i$, the norm of any tail $\sum_{j=p}^q a_{ji}$ is at most $L_B\theta^p\|x\|_N$, so the partial sums converge in the complete ring $A$, to $a_i$. Telescoping gives $x-x_{q+1}=\sum_i(\sum_{j=0}^q a_{ji})f_i$. Pass to the limit using the scalar-action bound and the finite sum: $x=\sum_i a_i f_i\in S$. Therefore $B=S$ and the image is closed.

source.place: Lemma 1, PDF p.1, read online 2026-10-24; agent expansion for bounded scalar actions, automatic continuity and the injective norm bound. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Suppose $u$ is injective. Its image $S$ with the norm inherited from $N$ is a Banach $K$-space by step 3: every Cauchy sequence converges in $N$ and closedness puts the limit in $S$. The corestriction $u:M\to S$ is continuous by step 2 and is surjective by the definition of $S$. Apply [lem-trf-banach-surjective-bounded-lifts] to obtain $H>0$ such that every $s\in S$ has a preimage $m'$ with $\|m'\|_M\le H\|s\|_N$. For $s=u(m)$, injectivity makes $m'=m$, giving $\|m\|_M\le H\|u(m)\|_N$ as required.

I traversed the 39 transitive dependencies of the three cited lemmas and the item is not among them, so there is no cycle. Step 2: the hypotheses of the bounded-lifts leaf (open mapping) are met: A^s is Banach because the quotient norm is a K-norm, M is Banach, and p is continuous by the c_M finite-sum bound. The estimate for u is correct. Step 3: B, the closure of S, is a complete A-submodule and is finite by the noetherian-submodule leaf (Stacks 00IK). I recomputed the perturbation: x_{j+1}=Σa_ji(b_i−f_i) with ‖x_{j+1}‖≤θ‖x_j‖ and ‖a_ji‖≤L_Bθ^j‖x‖. The nonarchimedean tails converge in A, and the limit gives x∈S. B=0 is handled. Step 4: S is Banach, the corestriction M→S is continuous and surjective, and injectivity gives H. Small cases: A=K finite-dimensional, multiplication by T on K<T> with H=1, and zero modules all hold.
